Fixes: integer overflow
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
fix_commit_message:
swscale/output: Use 64bit in addition in  yuv2gbrp16_full_X_c() for RGB + Y

Fixes: signed integer overflow: -1159988356 + -1082982400 cannot be represented in type 'int'
Fixes: 461519938/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_SWS_fuzzer-4777382021234688

Found-by:  continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d41b8d95a723 on top of intro b74f89caaef2 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): yuv2gbrp16_full_X_c() in libswscale/output.c converts YUV to planar 16-bit GBR(A) output. When commit b74f89caae reworked the 16bps output path to bias the calculations for a wider non-overflowing range, it introduced expressions of the form `av_clip_uintp2(((Y + R) >> 14) + (1<<15), 16)` where Y and R (also G, B) are both plain 32-bit signed `int` values whose magnitudes can individually approach INT32_MIN/MAX due to prior scaling/bias steps. Adding two such large-magnitude ints can overflow the 32-bit signed integer range, which is undefined behavior in C, and was found by OSS-Fuzz via UBSan (signed integer overflow: -1159988356 + -1082982400 cannot be represented in type 'int'). Root cause: The addition Y + R (and Y + G, Y + B) is performed entirely in 32-bit signed integer arithmetic even though the pre-scaled/biased Y value and the chroma-derived R/G/B values can each individually be close to the 32-bit signed integer limits, so their sum can exceed INT32_MAX or go below INT32_MIN, triggering undefined signed integer overflow.
